properties.content:
Report Details

Nearest City: Miami, FL
Location: 801 BRICKELL BAY DRIVE
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: UNKNOWN OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 25.765260, -80.188430 (Approximated from street_address)
Report Description
PER EMAIL: THERE ARE 3-4 MEDIUM BOATS (SAILBOATS, POWER BOATS) THAT ARE EITHER TOTALLY IMMERSED OR PARTIALLY SUNKEN IN THE SMALL MARINA NEXT TO BRICKELL KEY ( BRICKELL BAY DRIVE, MIAMI, FL 33131). I EVACUATED MY APARTMENT, SO I AM NOT SURE WHEN THOSE BOATS STARTED TO SINK. I RETURNED TO MY HOME ON WEDNESDAY 9/13 AND THAT IS WHEN I FIRST NOTICED THE BOATS AND DAMAGE TO THE AREA. THEN, ON SATURDAY 9/16/17, I OBSERVED SOME OIL-SHEEN FLOATING ON THE WATER AT AROUND 0900-11:30AM. IT ROUGHLY COVERED ABOUT 1,000 + SQ FT. THIS SURFACE POLLUTION APPEARS TO HAVE DISSIPATED FROM THE SURFACE, BUT THERE MAY BE MORE CONTAMINATION BECAUSE OF THE SUNKEN VESSELS (FUEL HOLDING TANKS, ETC). SEVERAL SMALL VESSELS TRAVELED ON THOSE CONTAMINATED WATERS AS WELL AS 2 DOLPHINS WHO WERE FEEDING NEARBY. I CALLED 311 TO REPORT IT TO THE COUNTY AND THEY SAID TO CONTACT YOU GUYS. I DID NOT TAKE A PICTURE AS I WAS ON HOLD FOR A LONG TIME... MY MISTAKE! I DO HAVE A PHOTO OF THE BOATS (ATTACHED). THE LONGER THOSE BOATS REMAIN IN THE WATER, MORE LIQUIDS WILL CONTINUE TO POLLUTE BRICKELL BAY AND ONE OF THE SAILBOATS KEEPS DRIFTING AND IS A NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD. I AM SURE YOU HAVE YOUR RESOURCES AT CAPACITY, BUT I WANTED TO REPORT THIS SO IT CAN MAKE THE LIST!

Reported Spill Volume: 495 gallon
Report Description/// UPDATE TO INCIDENT REPORT # 1381234 /// THE RP CONFIRMED 1875 LITRES OF DIESEL SPILLED TO GROUND THROUGH A CORRODED PLUG AT THE BOTTOM OF THE TANK. A QUALIFIED PROFESSIONAL (QP), ACTIVE EARTH ENGINEERING LTD., HAS PROVIDED AN INITIAL RESPONSE ASSESSMENT AND RECOMMENDATIONS. HARD AND SOFT FIXED BOOM REMAINS IN PLACE IN THE BAY AND CONTINUES TO BE EFFECTIVE CONTAINING ANY RECOVERABLE PRODUCT ON THE WATER. BOOM WILL REMAIN IN PLACE UNTIL MONITORING SHOWS NO ADDITIONAL CONTAMINATION. THE RP WILL CONTINUE TO USE ABSORBENT PADS, PARTICULARLY AT THE BASE OF THE ROCK EMBANKMENT UNTIL THE DIESEL STOPS SEEPING OUT IN THE AREA. THE QP BIOLOGIST HAS STATED THE AREA WILL RECOVER OVER TIME DUE TO PRODUCT EVAPORATION, ULTRAVIOLET DEGRADATION OF THE DIESEL, AND WAVE ACTION. RP WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR SOILS AND CHANGES TO VEGETATION AND WILDLIFE HEALTH WILL BE NOTED UNTIL THE AREA HAS RETURNED TO PREDISTURBANCE CONDITIONS. AS SPILL SITE CONDITIONS CONTINUE TO IMPROVE, CURRENT RESPONSE EFFORTS ARE EXPECTED TO TRANSITION TO RECOVERY FOR LONG-TERM MONITORING AND REMEDIATION EFFORTS. THE INCIDENT IS BEING DOWNGRADED TO CODE 1 NOTIFICATIONS, WITH NO FURTHER UPDATES EXPECTED. ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION: NEEC REPORT THE CALLER DISCOVERED THE DIESEL TANK HAD BEEN INTEREFERED WITH AND 3/4 OF THE TANK HAS BEEN PUMPED INTO THE TRINCOMALI CANAL.

Reported Spill Volume: 149610.39 gallons
Report Description
AT APPROXIMATELY 9:00AM ON FRIDAY, DECEMBER 23, 2011 THE FIRE DETECTION SYSTEM IN THE NUMBER 3 COMPRESSOR BUILDING AT THE CLIFTON COMPRESSOR STATION DETECTED A FIRE AND SHUT THE BUILDING DOWN. A BUILDING SHUTDOWN ISOLATES THE NATURAL GAS STREAM FROM THE TURBINE COMPRESSOR UNIT, BLOWS DOWN THE PIPING, SHUTS OFF ELECTRICAL POWER AND OTHER ANCILLARY EQUIPMENT RESULTING IN A RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS. EMPLOYEES SAW A SMALL FIRE UPON ARRIVAL AND SOME BLACK SMOKE. BOTH THE FIRE AND SMOKE STOPPED AS SOON AS THE SHUTDOWN WAS COMPLETE. AT THIS TIME, WE BELIEVE THAT THE FIRE WAS ELECTRICAL IN NATURE AND WHEN ELECTRICAL POWER WAS CUT, THE FIRE EXTINGUISHED.

THE ANOMALY HAD SOME WELL-DEFINED EDGES, STRONG CONTRAST, AND APPEARED OUT OF PLACE RESULTING IN MEDIUM-HIGH CONFIDENCE. UNCERTAINTIES: THIS ANOMALY MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH NUMEROUS NRC REPORTS OF AN UNKNOWN SHEEN ON 2 OCT, INCLUDING 1318492, 1318479, 1318486 AND 1318478, ONE OF WHICH INDICATED A 5 MI X 2 MI SHEEN. THESE NRC REPORTS WERE LOCATED EAST OF THE NORTHERN END OF THE CURRENT ANOMALY, SUGGESTING A POSSIBLE SLOW PROGRESSION OF THE ANOMALY TO THE WEST OVER TIME IF THEY ARE INDEED THE SAME ANOMALY. THE TRUCK DAMAGED ALL OF THE PIPING TO THE STORAGE TANK INCLUDING THE SHUT OFF VALVE. AS A RESULT OF THIS ACCIDENT GASOLINE RELEASED INTO SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AND WAS ONGOING DURING THE TIME OF THE REPORT. THE CALLER STATED EMERGENCY SERVICES ARE ON SCENE AND ARE DOUSING THE SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AREA WITH SUPPRESSION FOAM. WHEN THE REPORT WAS MADE THE CALLER ESTIMATED THAT 5000 GALLONS OF GASOLINE HAS BEEN RELEASED AND EXPECTS 8000-10000 GALLONS TO BE RELEASED OVER THE COURSE OF THIS EVENT. THE COMPLEX HAS BEEN EVACUATED AND THE ELECTRIC COMPANY IS ON SITE TO SHUT DOWN THE POWER. THE CALLER STATED THAT HAZMAT SERVICES IS CURRENTLY ONROUTE TO PUMP THE SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AREA AND THE REMAINDER OF WHAT IS IN THE STORAGE TANKS. THERE WERE NO INJURIES OR FATALITIES . THE FIRE DEPARTMENT EVACUATED EVERYONE IN A 1000 FOOT RADIUS.

Report Description\\ NOAA/NESDIS MPSR ISSUED FOR: GULF OF MEXICO \\ POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 05-16-2023 REPORT TIME: 1330 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: MAIN PASS MP0032 IMAGE DATE: 05-15-2023 IMAGE TIME: 1633 UTC DATA SOURCE: PLANETSCOPE MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 3 METER LOCATION: 29°27"37" N/89°24"54" W AREA: 3.26 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THE ANOMALY WAS 5.6 NM LONG AND .3 NM AT ITS WIDEST, AND APPEARED DARK WITH SHIMMERING AREAS CHARACTERISTIC OF THICKER OIL. THE ANOMALY WAS LOCATED IN THE MAIN PASS AREA APPROXIMATELY 5 NM OFF THE LOUISIANA COAST. IT APPEARED TO EMANATE FROM AN OIL FACILITY THAT WAS POSSIBLY THE SUBJECT OF NRC 1367300, TAKEN 5/15/2023. WINDS WERE N 6 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: THE ANOMALY WAS LOCATED IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO A CANAL OUTFALL, AND THE SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS MAY HAVE CONFUSED THE SIGNATURE OF DARKER OIL AND OVERALL EXTENT. ADDITIONALLY, BIOGENIC MATERIAL COULD NOT BE RULED OUT AS THE IMAGERY DID NOT ALLOW FOR VEGETATION TESTING. THESE TWO FACTORS MAY RESULT IN FALSE POSITIVES FOR OIL. THERE WERE ALSO MULTIPLE WELLS IN THE AREA SURROUNDING THE SUSPECTED SOURCE, BUT GIVEN THE NRC AND THICKER OIL SIGNATURE THE CONFIDENCE FOR THIS REPORT REMAINS HIGH. MAPS AND SHAPEFILES CAN BE ACCESSED AT: WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ ERMA: HTTPS://ERMA.NOAA.GOV/GULFOFMEXICO/ERMA.HTML#/LAYERS=1+51765&X=-89.3680455&Y=29.4416695&Z=11&PANEL=LAYER

SkyTruth Analysis

Reported Spill Volume: 0.25 gallons
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** AROUND 1400 HOURS, A PLANT MECHANIC CALLED HIS FOREMAN ON THE RADIO AND SAID THEY HAD AN OIL SPILL ON THE (LAKE COOLING WATER) INTAKE AND IT WAS HEADING FOR THE CIRCULATING WATER PUMP INLET. THE FOREMAN NOTIFIED 5 OTHER PEOPLE AND INFORMED THEM TO GET OIL PIGS AND HEAD TO THE INTAKE. THE FOREMAN CALLED ANOTHER INDIVIDUAL AND NOTIFIED HIM AND THEN WENT TO THE INTAKE. THE CREW INSTALLING 2B CIRCULATING WATER PUMP HAD BEEN PUMPING OIL IN TO THE MOTOR AND OVER FILLED IT. THE MOTOR IS ON THE EAST END NEXT TO THE NORTH HAND RAIL RIGHT NEXT TO THE STORM DRAIN. WE PLACE OIL PIGS IN THE WATER AND OIL MATS AROUND THE MOTOR AND IN THE DRAIN. WE THEN WENT TO THE DISCHARGE CHANNEL BUT COULD NOT FIND ANY SIGN OF OIL COMING OUT.
